parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 津波 (“tsunami”), from 津 (tsu, “harbour”) + 波 (nami, “wave”).
Borrowed from Japanese 柔(じゅう)術(じゅつ) (jūjutsu).

parole.significato: yen, Japanese monetary unit and coin
kanji (Chinese characters as used for the Japanese language)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 漢(かん)字(じ) (kanji, “Chinese characters”).

parole.significato: samurai (a member of a feudal Japanese warrior class)
parole.testo: Ultimately from Japanese 侍 (さむらい, samurai).

parole.significato: shogun (the supreme commander of the armed forces of feudal Japan)
parole.testo: Derived from Japanese 将軍 (shōgun), from an abbreviation of 征夷大将軍 (Seii Taishogun, “General who overcomes the barbarians”), from Middle Chinese 將軍 (tsjàng-kjun, “leader of troops, general”).
